passage:
Friday. Kashish packed her racket bag for the table-tennis final and told her mother, "Win or lose, I'll shake hands." Her stomach fluttered anyway.

Saturday. She lost to Sachin, three games to one. Her eyes stung and her legs felt heavy. She walked around the table, held out her hand and said, "Well played." It was hard to say. Sachin grinned, surprised. "Thanks. Your last serve was really tricky."

Monday. In class, two friends and even the sports teacher nodded at her. Kashish still felt a little sore about the loss, but steady too. At recess she asked Sachin to show her his backhand.

qa.q: Who did Kashish play in the table-tennis final?
What was Kashish feeling as she held out her hand to Sachin?
qa.a: It was hard for her, since her eyes stung and her legs felt heavy, but she still said "Well played."

qa.q: What could Kashish do next to improve after the loss?
qa.a: Learn from Sachin, for example by asking him to show his backhand, and keep practising.

qa.q: How might Sachin have felt when Kashish shook his hand?
qa.a: Surprised and pleased: he grinned and praised her last serve.

grounding: A child loses and still shakes hands and says well played, earning respect while accepting that wins and losses pass.

passage:
Coach's note, Sunday, inter-club table tennis.
Payal lost her semi-final to Pema, 11-9 in the fifth game. It was a close match, and Payal had led most of the way.
When the last point went, Payal stood still for a second. Her lip trembled. Then she walked round the table, shook Pema's hand and said, clearly, "Well played."
Several parents noticed. Pema's coach came over later to say how much they admired Payal's manner.
Afterwards Payal cried a little in the car park. I told her that the handshake was the bravest shot she played all day. We'll work on her fifth-game nerves this week.

qa.q: What was the score in the fifth game?
How did Payal feel right after losing?
qa.a: She felt deeply disappointed, with a trembling lip, and cried a little afterwards.
It showed good character in a hard moment and earned respect from parents and Pema's coach.

qa.q: How might Pema feel when Payal shakes her hand and says well played?
qa.a: Pema would likely feel respected and happy that her win was acknowledged graciously.

grounding: A girl loses a close match but still shakes hands and says well played, earning respect even though it is hard.

passage:
Sunday
Lost the carrom final to Zeenat today. 29-25. I was SO close. My eyes stung and I wanted to flick all the coins off the board.
But I remembered what Abbu says: the match ends, the person stays.
So I stood up and held out my hand. "Well played, Zeenat. That last rebound shot was amazing."
She smiled and shook it. "You nearly had me."
Some of the older boys clapped. Afterwards, the organiser uncle said I was a real sportsman.
I still feel rotten about losing. But I'm proud of how I lost.
Kamal

qa.q: What was the score in the carrom final?
How did Kamal feel right after losing?
qa.a: Kamal felt frustrated and upset, eyes stinging and wanting to flick the coins off the board.

qa.q: What did Kamal do that earned respect?
qa.a: Kamal shook Zeenat's hand and praised her last rebound shot.

qa.q: How might Zeenat feel when Kamal praises her shot?
qa.a: Zeenat seemed happy and gracious, saying Kamal nearly had her.

grounding: Kamal loses a carrom final but still shakes hands and says well played, which earns respect even though it feels hard.
